summary: Read one singly linked chain. Each node stores an integer and points at the next node. Reverse every successor arrow so the old tail becomes the new head and the old head becomes the new tail. Write the chain after that reversal. An empty chain stays empty. A chain of one node stays that same node. Integers stored in the nodes stay unchanged; only the arrows move. Walking from the new head to the new tail visits the integers in the opposite order from the chain you read.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is a node count followed by the integer stored in each node.
